feed.title: PGM Lab
feed.subtitle: The Laboratory for Precision Genome Medicine (PGM Lab) at Yonsei University College of Medicine conducts translational research at the intersection of human genetics and precision medicine, integrating wet-lab and computational approaches to improve disease diagnosis and treatment.

entry.title: Photo: Lab life in 2026, 2nd semester
entry.content:
Moments from lab life during the second semester of 2026.

Prof. Dongwon Lee from Harvard Medical School and the Broad Institute visited our lab.

During lunch with Prof. Dongwon Lee,

entry.title: PGM Lab 2026 Year-End Workshop 🎄
entry.content:
The PGM Lab 2026 Year-End Workshop will be held on December 17, 2026 (Thu), 13:30–17:55, in the B1 conference room of the Visa Examination Center at Gangnam Severance Hospital.

We will look back on 2026 and share our plans for 2027.

Lab members will present their work on nanopore sequencing in neuromuscular disease and hereditary neuropathy, as well as AI in laboratory medicine.
Tadeas will share his experience as a visiting student in Korea, and Garam Lee will introduce herself as our newest member.

To close the day, our alumnus Ayoub El Bakiallah (PhD student, EMBL) will join via Zoom to talk about genomic and epigenomic signatures of aging from high-coverage nanopore whole-genome sequencing.

Limited-edition workshop mug ☕

To celebrate our first year workshop, every attendee will get a limited-edition PGM Lab mug as a present.
The Christmas tree is built from nanopore membranes, with a DNA strand threading through each pore.
The ornaments are nucleotides and base modifications (5mC, 5hmC, 6mA), and the trunk is a raw nanopore squiggle.

The sequence running down the tree hides a message, encoded as A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3 in 8-bit ASCII.
Can you decode it? 🎄

entry.title: PGM Lab @ The 35th International KOGO Annual Conference

link.title: PGM Lab @ The 35th International KOGO Annual Conference

entry.content:
Our lab spent 3rd–5th, September at the Sejong University Convention Center for the 35th International KOGO Annual Conference.
Great sessions, good discussions with colleagues across the genomics community, and a chance for our members to present and get feedback on their work.

Thanks to KOGO for another well-run meeting — and to our team for making the trip a fun one.

📍 Sejong University Convention Center, Seoul
🗓️ 2026.09.03–09.05

Jongung presented his work on computational predictions of all possible missense variants in CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 using protein language models.

Tadeas attended his first conference in Korea — here in front of Moon Young’s poster. 😂

entry.title: 2026 Nanopore User Group Meeting Seoul
entry.content:
Last Thursday, our lab members attended the 2026 Oxford Nanopore User Group Meeting in Seoul, held at the Dragon City Hotel in Yongsan.
The program featured six invited speakers from a wide range of fields, showcasing how nanopore sequencing is being applied across the spectrum from basic science to clinical practice.
Our group was also given the opportunity to present our ongoing work 🧬, including whole-genome sequencing of 56 Korean individuals.

The venue was excellent and the meeting drew a large, engaged crowd.
Beyond the talks, it was a great chance to network with many researchers working with nanopore technology and exchange ideas across disciplines,
and the lunch 🍽️ was also great.
We came away with plenty of inspiration for the projects ahead.

Last but not least — it was also Sophia Sim’s final day interning with us.
We hope your time here was a good one, and we’ll be keeping our 🤞 fingers crossed for your next step.
Best of luck, Sophia!

entry.title: New Faces and a Fond Farewell 🌱

link.title: New Faces and a Fond Farewell 🌱

entry.content:
Last Friday, our lab members enjoyed a memorable outing to Mt. Namsan and Itaewon for a combined farewell and welcome celebration.

While we are sad to see our first lab member, Ayoub, leave for the next chapter of his academic journey in Germany, 🥲
we are excited for the opportunities ahead of him.
We are confident that he will thrive in his PhD program at EMBL and wish him every success in his future endeavors.

At the same time, we are delighted to welcome Dr. Haeun Kim to our lab.
Dr. Kim earned her PhD in Chemistry from Yonsei University, and we look forward to her contributions and collaborations within the group.

We also warmly welcomed our summer internship students, Sophia and Mandalmaa, who will be joining us for the coming months.
We hope their time in the lab will be both enjoyable and rewarding.

One of the highlights of the day was our first experience trying Moroccan cuisine 🍲 together.
It was a unique and memorable cultural experience for everyone.

Thank you, Ayoub, for your dedication, friendship, and valuable contributions to the lab.
We wish you all the best in Germany and look forward to following your future achievements.
entry.summary: Last Friday, our lab members enjoyed a memorable outing to Mt. Namsan and Itaewon for a combined farewell and welcome celebration.

entry.title: Our Lab T-Shirt 👕 is ready 👊👊
entry.content:
The lab now has the first version of its own T-shirt, and we could not be more excited to wear it!

“SEQUENCING LIFE” is our humorous slogan for everyday lab life.

Printed in crisp white on deep navy, the front lays out what we do every day as a five-step pipeline:

PIPETTE ADDICTED → GENOME SEQUENCING → DNA IS OUR CODE → LINUX POWERED → DATA NEVER SLEEPS,

complete with a pipette, a nanopore sequencer, a DNA double helix, the Linux penguin, and a humming server.

Below the icons, a progress bar reads

LOADING GENOMES… 99% — a wink at every analysis that is almost done but somehow always needs one more run. 😄

It carries the PGM Lab name and our motto, “Decoding the Genomes, Transforming Patient Care,” showing the playful design back to what we actually do every day.

I designed this 2026 edition of our lab T-shirt so we could carry a little of the joy of scientific discovery with us wherever we go.

I hope this t-shirt stays with each of you as a small token of the time we shared decoding genomes together.

A small thing, but a fun way to show some lab spirit — and a reminder that behind every variant call there is a team that loves this work. 🤣
entry.summary: The lab now has the first version of its own T-shirt, and we could not be more excited to wear it!

entry.title: Thursday Lab Meeting — Allele-Specific Methylation Analysis in the Nanopore WGS dataset 🧬

link.title: Thursday Lab Meeting — Allele-Specific Methylation Analysis in the Nanopore WGS dataset 🧬

entry.content:
At this week’s Thursday lab meeting, Ayoub presented his ongoing analysis of allele-specific methylations (ASM) in 48 Korean genomes profiled by Oxford Nanopore long-read whole-genome sequencing.

Leveraging the CpG methylation signals natively available from ONT data, Ayoub walked us through his established pipeline for phasing methylation onto haplotypes and identifying loci with allelic imbalance across the cohort.

He shared new findings from the dataset, including novel ASM regions as well as validation of previously reported loci, illustrating how integrating methylation and haplotype information sharpens the resolution at which regulatory variation can be pinpointed in a population-scale Korean dataset.

Thanks Ayoub for the interesting presentation, and to everyone who joined the lively discussion afterward — looking forward to seeing where this work leads! 🚀
